name: Nordic hamstring curl
pattern: Eccentric knee flexion: kneeling with the ankles held, the body lowers forward as one straight line while the hamstrings brake the fall.
setup: Kneel on a pad; a partner, bar or strap holds your ankles.
Body straight from knees to head, hips locked, arms ready in front of the chest.
Squeeze glutes and brace before you start.

steps.text: Lean forward slowly from the knees, keeping hips straight.
Resist as long as you can as the hamstrings start to give way.
Catch yourself with your hands, chest near the floor.
Push off lightly with the hands and curl back up with the hamstrings.

cues.cue: Hips straight: knees, hips and shoulders in a line.
cues.why: With neutral hips the long head of biceps femoris works hard near full knee extension; bending at the hips changes the exercise.

cues.cue: Fall as slowly as you can, 3-5 seconds.
cues.why: The value is in the slow eccentric braking.

cues.cue: Try to push the break point lower each week.
cues.why: The angle where you lose control marks how strong the hamstrings are eccentrically.
Programmes including the Nordic cut hamstring injuries by about half.

breathing: Breathe in at the top, slow steady breath out while lowering.

tempo.note: As slow as you can on the way down.

mistakes.name: Hips bend
mistakes.looks: The buttocks push back and the chest drops while the thighs stay upright.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze glutes; think of a plank falling forward.
mistakes.why: Bending at the hips shortens the lever and shifts work from the biceps femoris.

mistakes.name: Fast drop
mistakes.looks: You lower a little, then fall to the floor.
mistakes.fix: Use a band or a slope for help so you can control the whole range.
mistakes.why: Little eccentric work after the break point.

mistakes.name: Low back arches
mistakes.looks: The belly sags toward the floor during the descent.
mistakes.fix: Brace your abs as for a plank.
mistakes.why: The trunk is not stiff, so the line breaks.

safety: Expect strong soreness the first weeks; start with 1-2 sets of 3-5.
Recent hamstring strain: wait until cleared and pain-free.

variants.change: Band from above pulls the chest up: lower further under control.
On a glute-ham bench: start horizontal and curl up with the knees, hips straight.
One leg: similar torque and muscle activity per leg.
Hips bent 90°: higher knee torque, more semitendinosus at a longer length.

harder: full nordic curl with no hands

subtypes.name: Glute-ham raise
subtypes.change: Thighs on the pad of a glute-ham bench; from a horizontal body, curl up until upright, hips straight.

metrics.label: Break point (knee bend)
metrics.good: lower is stronger; about 55-60 is common

motion.basis: Rigid-body lowering: trunk = 90 - knee flexion with hips at 0. sconce2021 reports break-point angles of about 120-126°, which we read as the thigh-to-shank angle (so about 55-60° of knee flexion); this reading is our interpretation. Catch pose and arm angles are estimates.
